name: a-hello-with-a-wrong-token-closes-4001
description: A hello whose token is not the listener's is answered auth_failed and closed with 4001; a right hello behind it in the same read is not read. A hello with no token is bad_hello and closes with 1002.
reason: The token is the only thing standing between a local process and the app's intents (HK-257).
verifiedBy: DESIGN.md v1.4, v1.7; docs/protocol.md spec v0. Rust: rust/powerup-core/tests/listener.rs listener_scenarios plays every step through protocol::listener::Listener. Swift: ProtocolServerTests drives the same rules over a real loopback socket.

steps.reason: Settings start the listener: the start stops first (generation 1), then binds 127.0.0.1 with generation 2 (RemoteListener.swift:79-135).
The bind is ready: running, no problem (RemoteListener.swift:158-161).
A socket is accepted: it becomes connection 1 under the 15-second deadline (RemoteListener.swift:222-257, 427-433).

bytes.text:
GET /ws HTTP/1.1
Host: 127.0.0.1:48738
Upgrade: websocket
Connection: Upgrade
Sec-WebSocket-Key: dGhlIHNhbXBsZSBub25jZQ==
Sec-WebSocket-Version: 13

steps.reason: A wrong token: auth_failed, then close 4001 (RemoteListener.swift:681-688).

effects.http:
HTTP/1.1 101 Switching Protocols
Upgrade: websocket
Connection: Upgrade
Sec-WebSocket-Accept: s3pPLMBiTxaQ9kYGzzhZRbK+xOo=

message.message: The token doesn't match — copy it from Settings → Remote → Read-back.

steps.reason: A socket is accepted: it becomes connection 2 under the 15-second deadline (RemoteListener.swift:222-257, 427-433).

steps.reason: A wrong hello, then a right one in the same read: the connection is closing after the first, so the second is not read (Swift read it, and could authenticate a connection it had refused; the core does not).
